definitions.explanation: The middle value in a data set when all values are arranged in order. A statistical measure used as an alternative to the average because it is less affected by extreme values.

examples.japanese: {年収|ねんしゅう}の{中央値|ちゅうおうち}は{約|やく}400{万円|まんえん}だ。
examples.english: The median annual income is approximately 4 million yen.

examples.japanese: {平均値|へいきんち}より{中央値|ちゅうおうち}の{方|ほう}が{実態|じったい}を{反映|はんえい}している。
examples.english: The median reflects the actual situation better than the average.

examples.japanese: {住宅|じゅうたく}{価格|かかく}の{中央値|ちゅうおうち}が{前年|ぜんねん}より{上昇|じょうしょう}した。
examples.english: The median housing price rose compared to the previous year.

notes:
A statistical term composed of {中央|ちゅうおう} (center; middle) and {値|ち} (value). The {中央値|ちゅうおうち} is frequently used in news and economic reporting because, unlike the {平均値|へいきんち} (mean/average), it is not skewed by extremely high or low values. This makes it especially useful for income, housing prices, and other data with uneven distributions.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {年収|ねんしゅう}の{中央値|ちゅうおうち}: median income
- {中央値|ちゅうおうち}を{求|もと}める: to calculate the median
- {中央値|ちゅうおうち}と{平均値|へいきんち}: median and average

RELATED WORDS:
- {平均値|へいきんち}: average; mean — the sum of all values divided by the count
- {最頻値|さいひんち}: mode — the most frequently occurring value in a data set
- {偏差値|へんさち}: deviation score — a standardized score used heavily in Japanese education
